name: Ochall Ochne

attributes.attribute: killed each other at the epic's end

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ochall Ochne was an Irish mythological figure. He was a Fairy king of Connacht in the west. Within the Tain Bo Cuailnge he played a small part. His swineherd Rucht held an endless argument with Friuch, a fellow swineherd. The pair passed through many rebirths until they took shape as the two great bulls. Those bulls killed each other at the epic's close.

okr.objective: Ochall Ochne is a Connacht Fairy king of small part in the Tain.
key_results: He rules as a Fairy king of western Connacht.
His swineherd Rucht argued without end with Friuch.
The pair were reborn until they became two great bulls.
Those bulls killed each other as the epic closed.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
